industry.why: Neutral, carried, balanced on new evidence both ways. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment and grid, Diversified groups, Distributors and Test and measurement at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Counter-case for B: the order data are the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack; for D: the tape and the regime.

sector.why: Neutral, set deliberately this week (carried C). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): diversified industrial groups are cyclical capital goods into a growth scare, but their diversification is itself the simple, proven profile the regime pays for, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: A now, C prior, says the market is paying for it. Three memos this week in this Sector all turn on the Fragility axis, not on the Sector: Beijer Alma (Mixed) and Idun Industrier (Fights it) are small, geared, re-rating-dependent Swedish acquirers, thyssenkrupp (Mixed) is large but 'neither simple nor proven'; the Fragility row carries that judgement, so the Sector row does not double it. One live holding, Sdiptech (5.05%, Sell-side and Thematic Fit A). Counter-case for higher: leadership and six MI Pool names with Thematic Fit B; for lower: the group's small acquirers are what a credit crack hurts first. Neutral by judgement.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium (firm on the price, a working hypothesis on the modal path). A park on price, not an invalidation. The park rule fires twice: 'Business' (E 2, BB 2) is D and 'Transmission' (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) is D; management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) is C and trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) is B; the record does not argue against the park because the two D's are the reasons the modal return cannot be trusted to within a third of earnings. Conditions that progress the case: a price near the 200-day average (EUR 11.27; the three-year bar clears at EUR 10.76 on the modal path) after the tk accelis listing, with Q4 FY2026 Steel Europe EBITDA per tonne above EUR 50 at the results on 8 December 2026; or, at any price, a defined Steel Europe separation with the pensions allocated away from the parent, which would move the multiple anchor to 11.5x and 'Foundations' to C. Invalidate triggers: cumulative cuts below 7,000 by September 2027; hot-rolled coil below EUR 650 per tonne for two quarters; net cash below EUR 1.5bn at FY2026/27 year-end without separation funding; a separation timeline beyond mid-2027 without legal structure or external funding.
case: - The thesis: thyssenkrupp is a self-help and break-up case in a weak business, not a demand inflection and not a compounder. A chief executive with a mandate to May 2031 is dismantling a loss-making conglomerate into listed parts and cutting the cost base of its weakest part by a third under a signed labour agreement, while EU trade policy lifts the price that weakest part receives. At EUR 13.695 the shares have already paid for the two parts sold and the agreement signed; the third part, a standalone Steel Europe, has no date and no structure, and without it the modal return is about 15 percent a year over eighteen months and about 11 percent over three years, below the 20 percent bar. In one line: a new management can sell the market the parts of a conglomerate faster than its steel business consumes the cash; at EUR 13.70 the market has paid for the two parts already sold and the third has no date.

- The change is internal, broad and dated (E 1, BB 1 B; RA 2 B). Seven of twelve internal forces at B or better: strategy change A (ACES 2030, a financial holding of independent segments; TKMS listed; tk accelis approved; Steel Europe to be made standalone with the parent possibly a minority holder, structure undefined); perimeter reduction A (HKM, Automation Engineering, Electrical Steel India, two 49 percent listings, the shipment target cut); the labour agreement B; chief executive B (novelty spent after three years; a restructuring record, not a growth one; SGL's carbon-fibre business deteriorated after he left); guidance raised B (floor lift, with sales guidance cut and Automotive cut about 30 percent); standards improvement B (APEX more than 2,500 measures and more than EUR 2bn over two years; sceptics say savings pass to customers); shareholder returns B (the dividend in kind). Balance-sheet utilisation D is the one force moving against the case. The screen's false-positive checks: no caretaker, no 'PowerPoint transformation', a trivial guidance rise partly, crown jewels sold historically, no empire-building, no dangerous leverage, no debt-funded buyback.

- The external forces net to a C (RA 1, E 1, BB 1): political and regulatory A (the strongest single external force, a tailwind to price and utilisation toward 80 to 85 percent mill operating rates); competition B (easing by policy at the border, not in the mill); the company's own cycle B (turning from a deep trough, cost- and policy-led); demand D (automotive about 50 percent of Steel Europe volumes and 20 percent of Materials Services sales; recovery pushed to 2027 or later at low plausibility; construction down 9 percent since 2022; EU flat-steel consumption projected stable to 2030); supply side D (German energy among the highest globally; coking coal USD 263 per tonne; low Rhine water in July 2026 cut Duisburg port loading to a third; energy commitments EUR 1.0bn, iron ore EUR 780m); disruption D (green hydrogen later and dearer; the plant on gas); macroeconomic D (negative natural hedge); catch-all C (French sovereign and credit stress bears on the listing window).
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, the bull case at its strongest: the street under-models Steel Europe and the July 2026 safeguards are a structural change the market has not capitalised. Deutsche Bank sits 2 to 23 percent above consensus adjusted EBIT for FY2026 to FY2028 and models Steel Europe EBITDA of EUR 1.5bn against the company's EUR 1.2bn target and Morgan Stanley's EUR 1.13bn; the Capital Markets Day target itself is 27 percent above the Visible Alpha consensus of EUR 0.94bn; Deutsche Bank says the self-help potential is "heavily underestimated by the broader street" and expects the company "comfortably at the upper end" of EUR 0.60bn to 0.90bn. Hot-rolled coil at EUR 800 per tonne with Europe short 10 to 15 million tonnes drives, on Morgan Stanley's arithmetic, significant consensus EBITDA upgrades if the price holds. The tk accelis listing crystallises EUR 1 to 3 per share above street expectations; the pension liability halves on a Steel Europe deconsolidation (Jefferies); Morgan Stanley's bull-case sum-of-the-parts is EUR 24.70, 80 percent above the price. The record concedes: the policy change is the largest in European steel's competitive field in a decade and is not fully in the FY2027 estimates; more than half of the EUR 800m self-help is contractual; the listing is dated and approved; the fair multiple on a completed break-up is 11.5x, not 9.0x, and that return is shown (33.5 percent a year at eighteen months, 19.3 percent at three years). The record holds its view because the two contractual legs are already in a price that has risen 65 percent to the 88th percentile of its five-year multiple range; the leg that moves the multiple to 11.5x has failed twice and has no date (0.40 even after a successful listing; 0.30 in all); a third of the earnings can leak from an unguided chain (55.6 percent reported tax; 49 percent minorities on two subsidiaries and 49.8 percent of nucera; EUR 544m of special items in nine months); and net cash is down EUR 2.3bn in nine months. Where the case against would win: a stated ownership target, external funding and pension allocation for Steel Europe, the single event that moves the anchor to 11.5x and 'Foundations' to C.

- The bear's case, also not taken: the risks research's "NO profile", a EUR 11.36bn structural burden exceeding the market capitalisation, sets gross liabilities against equity while ignoring EUR 2.6bn of net cash and the operating value of the listed parts; its two hard inconsistencies, that the listing and the signed agreement would not happen, are exactly the things that have happened. The record makes no "covers the enterprise value" claim, because the files do not carry the listed market value of TKMS or an equity value for tk accelis; the brokers' sum-of-the-parts (Morgan Stanley base EUR 14.50, in line with the price; Jefferies with a 20 percent discount) is their assertion, cited as such.
triggers: - Progress: a price near the 200-day average (EUR 11.27; the three-year bar clears at EUR 10.76) after the tk accelis listing, with Q4 FY2026 Steel Europe EBITDA per tonne above EUR 50 on 8 December 2026; or, at any price, a defined Steel Europe separation (ownership target, external funding, pension allocation of EUR 2.7bn away from the parent), which moves the multiple anchor to 11.5x and 'Foundations' to C.

- Invalidate: cumulative cuts below 7,000 by September 2027; northern European hot-rolled coil below EUR 650 per tonne for two quarters; net cash below EUR 1.5bn at FY2026/27 year-end without separation funding; a separation timeline beyond mid-2027 without legal structure or external funding; the tk accelis listing below EUR 2.5bn enterprise value.

- Alarm: Steel Europe EBITDA per tonne below EUR 45 in two consecutive quarters; hot-rolled coil below EUR 750 per tonne for a quarter; the listing slipping beyond Q1 2027; a quarter in which net cash falls below EUR 2.0bn without a transaction explaining it.

- What would change the side taken on each thing the case turns on: self-help, EBITDA per tonne below EUR 45 for two quarters or cuts below 7,000 by September 2027; hot-rolled coil, below EUR 650 for two quarters or a safeguard review; the re-rating branch, a stated ownership target, external funding and pension allocation for Steel Europe; the drop-through, a stated post-listing earnings-per-share bridge from the company or the brokers; the cash cushion, a quarter with net cash below EUR 2.0bn without a transaction.

- Open gaps: whether consensus FY2027 and FY2028 earnings per share deduct the 49 percent tk accelis minority (unstated in every input; our path deducts it); the drawn amount of the EUR 1.7bn facility (not in the files); the consensus treatment of special items; the Steel Europe pension allocation (EUR 2.4bn to EUR 2.7bn at different dates; EUR 2.7bn used); the 83-month foreign-currency hedge horizon with USD 944m outside hedge accounting, unsized; the firm's own track-record and lessons files not in the folder; no live thematics file or ticker sidecar in the folder; the sector tilt missing from the weekly thematic run; the listed market value of TKMS and an equity value for tk accelis absent, so no enterprise-value cover is claimed.

- Near-term dated events: BaFin prospectus approval mid-October 2026; tk accelis register entry and Prime Standard listing late October 2026 (the ex-date removes about EUR 1.50 per share from thyssenkrupp's price; add the distributed shares back before judging a mark-to-market move); FY2025/26 results 8 December 2026 (Q4 Steel Europe EBITDA per tonne; the low-three-digit-million HKM exit charge; maintenance shutdowns); January 2027 contract resets on 15 to 20 percent of Steel Europe volumes; quarterly quota drawdown data; first tk accelis standalone results; 7,000 cumulative cuts by fiscal 2027; KONE and TK Elevator as a valuation anchor; the HKM slab contract expiry in 2028; the tk accelis first dividend in 2028; the direct reduction plant's start-up on gas; the 2030 labour agreement end-point.
